content: The Chronic Care Model (CCM), as endorsed by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), provides a structured approach for the management of chronic diseases such as diabetes. It emphasizes six fundamental components: 1. Delivery System Design: This involves creating a proactive and coordinated care system that ensures patients receive timely and organized medical attention. 2. Self-Management Support: Patients are empowered with the tools, education, and resources necessary to actively manage their own health and make informed decisions about their care. 3. Decision Support: Healthcare providers are guided by evidence-based clinical guidelines to ensure that medical decisions are effective and aligned with the latest research. 4. Clinical Information Systems: These systems utilize patient registries to track and manage patient data, enabling better monitoring and follow-up care. 5. Community Resources: External resources are integrated to promote and sustain healthy lifestyle choices, supporting patients beyond the clinical setting. 6. Health Systems: The focus is on fostering a culture within healthcare organizations that prioritizes quality improvement and patient-centered care.
